extracted.intended_audience: stakeholders and members of the public preparing comments on HUD proposed rules (PHAs, owners, advocates, researchers, practitioners)
extracted.subtask_description: Identify opportunities and substantive topics for public comment on Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) proposed rules and related notices, including listening sessions, methodologies, program changes, and implementation details that commenters should address.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of reopened public comment
rubrics_metrics.description: This supplemental notice of proposed rulemaking re-opens public comment for certain topics and provisions that were addressed in HUD's May 29, 2024, proposed rule entitled "HOME Investment Partnerships Program: Program Updates and Streamlining."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters should identify which specific topics/provisions from the earlier proposal are being re-opened and focus input on those matters; distinguish new arguments from ones previously submitted. When a supplemental NPRM re-opens comment, tailor responses to the newly-identified topics rather than re-submitting general comments already on the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solicitation of comments on methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: This document announces a solicitation of comments on the methodology described to determine the Section 108 loan guarantee fee to cover credit subsidy costs that HUD published in the Federal Register on November 19, 2025.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments should address the methodology (assumptions, data sources, calculations, statutory consistency), including whether the fee accurately offsets credit subsidy costs and any alternatives. Point to specific methodological steps and provide evidence or data where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of public listening sessions as a commenting mechanism
rubrics_metrics.description: HUD will host three, two-part virtual public listening sessions to allow interested persons an opportunity to learn about and provide comments on the "HOME Investment Partnerships Program: Program Updates and Streamlining." The Part 1 listening sessions will address ... community housing development organizations, maximum subsidy amounts, green building incentives, homebuyer housing, and community land trusts. The Part 2 listening sessions will address ... rental housing, tenant-based rental assistance, and tenant protections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attend/listen to the session most aligned with your issue; prepare concise oral remarks focused on the listed topics; reference the part/topic you address. Use sessions to highlight evidence, local impacts, or implementation concerns and to signal willingness to submit more detailed written comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment period extensions and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: HUD has extended comment periods in at least one case (e.g., a 9-day extension for a proposed rule) and re-opened comment opportunities via supplemental notices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always check the specific document for the current comment deadline (including extensions or supplemental reopenings). If a rule re-opens comment on particular topics, focus additional submissions on those topics and note prior submissions if relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: PHAS scoring: emphasize measurable outcomes and available data
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed revisions would revise the weight of PHAS performance indicators to emphasize the importance of occupancy, financial condition, and physical assessments. To the greatest extent possible, scoring indicators would be based on measurable program outcomes and data that is already available to HUD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments on PHAS should evaluate proposed indicator weights, the choice of measurable outcomes, data availability/quality, and potential unintended consequences. Provide empirical evidence, suggest alternate metrics, and assess administrative burden of new measurements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to consider multiple sources, recency, and relevance in criminal-history decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed revisions would require that prior to any discretionary denial or termination for criminal activity, PHAs and assisted housing owners take into consideration multiple sources of information, including but not limited to the recency and relevance of prior criminal activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters should address what sources should be considered, how to operationalize recency/relevance, safeguards against discrimination, and impacts on program safety and access. Provide model policies or statutory interpretations where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification of eligible immigration/citizenship status for all applicants and recipients
rubrics_metrics.description: This proposed rule would revise HUD's Section 214 implementing regulations to require the verification of U.S. citizenship or the eligible immigration status of all applicants and recipients of assistance under a covered program regardless of age. The proposed rule would also make prorated assistance a temporary condition pending verification of eligible status of all family members, where permitted by statute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments should address verification procedures, privacy/data protections, timelines for verification, effects of provisional/prorated assistance, statutory authority, and administrative burden. Supply evidence on likely impacts to vulnerable populations and recommendations to minimize harm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment with OMB guidance for federal financial assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: HUD is proposing to amend its regulations on Federal financial assistance to conform with 2020 and 2024 changes to Office of Management and Budget (OMB) guidance. Proposed changes include adopting consistent and standardized terms and data elements, implementing data- and risk-based frameworks, and clarifying SAM.gov registration and audit requirements for certain loan guarantee programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments should assess whether proposed conforming changes properly implement OMB guidance, whether data elements are appropriate and minimize burden, how SAM.gov and audit requirements affect recipients, and whether risk-based frameworks are defensible and transparent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adoption of updated statistical/geographic standards requires public comment on program purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: This proposed rule would adopt the 2020 Core Based Statistical Area (CBSA) standards as determined by OMB. The MAPS Act requires agencies that propagate OMB's CBSA Standards for non-statistical use to seek public comment before determining that the propagation supports the purposes of the agency's programs and is in the public interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments should explain how adopting the updated CBSA standards would (or would not) support HUD program purposes, including data accuracy, program administration, and local impacts. Provide program-specific examples demonstrating benefits or harms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposals that change substantive legal/regulatory tests warrant legal and evidentiary comment
rubrics_metrics.description: HUD is proposing to remove its discriminatory effects regulations and leave to courts questions related to interpretations of disparate impact liability under the Fair Housing Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a proposal alters HUD's legal standards (e.g., removing a regulatory test), commenters should provide legal analysis, cite case law, discuss potential enforcement gaps, and present evidence on likely civil-rights outcomes. Address whether HUD's withdrawal raises compliance uncertainty and propose alternatives if desired.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program-specific operational flexibilities and limits (e.g., HOME per-unit subsidy and green-building incentives)
rubrics_metrics.description: This supplemental NPRM proposes to revise or revoke previously-proposed tenant protection provisions permitting participating jurisdictions to exceed the maximum per-unit subsidy for projects that met certain green building standards, and would create additional flexibilities related to scattered site manufactured housing rental projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments should address tradeoffs between subsidy limits and green-building incentives, impacts on affordability and environmental goals, and whether proposed flexibilities for manufactured housing are sufficient. Provide cost estimates, program impact analysis, or alternative policy proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposals to permit optional local policies (e.g., work requirements/term limits)
rubrics_metrics.description: This proposed rule would amend HUD regulations to provide PHAs and certain Multifamily Housing Owners with the option to implement work requirements for work-eligible adults and term limits for non-elderly, non-disabled families receiving specified assistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters should evaluate the evidence on effectiveness, potential harms, local flexibility vs. federal standards, administrative feasibility, and statutory fit. Provide empirical studies, local data, or recommended guardrails to protect vulnerable households.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational changes affecting mortgage/mortgagor funds disbursement
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed rule would permit mortgagees to disburse up to 1 percent of the mortgage amount initially endorsed for insurance before requiring that the funds provided by the mortgagor be disbursed in full, to allow pooling into mortgage-backed securities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments should address risks to borrowers and HUD insurance funds, transparency, timing, and whether the change would create incentives that affect borrower protections. Provide analysis of financial impacts and suggested consumer protections if approving such a change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rescission or removal of program requirements (e.g., Affirmative Fair Housing Marketing regulations)
rubrics_metrics.description: This proposed rule would rescind the Department's Affirmative Fair Housing Marketing regulations, which require a participant in an FHA insurance or Multifamily Housing rental assistance program to complete and submit a form supplied by HUD describing its affirmative fair housing marketing plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When HUD proposes to rescind a requirement, comments should examine the consequences for fair housing outreach and enforcement, alternatives to maintain fair marketing, and whether rescission will reduce or increase compliance burdens on recipients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tester eligibility and fairness in testing programs
rubrics_metrics.description: HUD published a proposed rule 'Removing Criminal Conviction Restrictions for Testers in FHIP- and FHAP-Funded Testing Programs,' proposing to eliminate tester restrictions that forbid use of fair housing testers with prior felony convictions or convictions of crimes involving fraud or perjury.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments should address whether removing tester restrictions affects the quality or credibility of testing, statutory or programmatic constraints, rehabilitation considerations, and program effectiveness in detecting discrimination. Provide operational recommendations for vetting testers if changes are adopted.
